clinician.trajectory_summary: A 61-year-old Syrian male with alcoholism and heavy smoking presented with a 3-year history of pruritic hyperpigmented patches localized to the right trunk and right thigh without telangiectasias, scaling, or atrophy. Initial workup revealed slight leukocytosis. Skin biopsy demonstrated parakeratotic hyperkeratotic epidermis with spongiosis and a papillary dermal infiltrate of atypical lymphocytes arranged in clusters and linear basilar distribution along the dermoepidermal junction with melanophage deposition. Immunohistochemistry confirmed a cytotoxic T-cell phenotype (CD3+, CD8+, CD4-, CD20-). Systemic staging with chest and abdomen CT showed no lymphadenopathy or organomegaly, confirming early stage disease. The patient was treated with psoralen and ultraviolet A (PUVA) therapy twice weekly plus topical 0.1% betamethasone dipropionate. After 12 weeks, he achieved partial response with relief of pruritus and regression of hyperpigmentation, though lesions did not completely disappear. Molecular studies (TCR gene rearrangement), EBV testing (EBER ISH, serology, PCR), cytotoxic markers (TIA-1, perforin, granzyme B), CD56, CD7, and bone marrow biopsy were not documented in the source record.
